newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal state TV signs new deal with government.
newsitem.headline: Portugal state TV signs new deal with government.

text.p: Portugal's loss-making state owned RTP television company has signed a new deal with the government under which it gets a 10 billion escudo ($64 million) capital boost while accepting limits on advertising.
The government said that the capital rise would "ensure the financial equilibrium" of the loss-making concern and allow it to make new investments.
The company, which operates two television channels, will reduce the level of advertising on its main RTP1 network and cut out commercial spots altogether from RTP2.
It will be obliged to dedicate every year 26 hours of broadcast time each to theatre, documentaries and works of fiction by Portuguese authors.
The new contract emphasised RTP's role as a public service, secretary of state for the media, Alberto Arons de Carvalho, said in a statement on Monday night.
RTP1 has been fighting a losing battle in the ratings with the SIC commercial station of media tycoon and former prime minister Francisco Pinto Balsemao.
SIC specialises in Brazilian soap operas and games programmes.
